components.note: 发 (fā) gives a sound related to fèi, sharing the initial f-, though the rhyme has drifted from ā to èi over time.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这个旧电视已经是废物了,该扔掉了。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiù diànshì yǐjīng shì fèiwù le, gāi rēngdiào le.
example.english: This old television is already junk; it's time to throw it out.
example.fact: Recycling a single aluminum can saves enough energy to power a television for about three hours, because turning scrap aluminum back into new metal takes only about 5% of the energy needed to refine it from raw ore. That gap is why aluminum is one of the most economically worthwhile materials to recycle.

components.note: 日 here pictures a person's head.
共 pictures two hands; together with the shape below, they depict a violent struggle, giving 暴 its meaning 'violent, sudden.'
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.

example.hanzi: 调查最终暴露了公司的财务问题。
example.pinyin: Diàochá zuìzhōng bàolù le gōngsī de cáiwù wèntí.
example.english: The investigation ultimately exposed the company's financial problems.
example.fact: X-rays were discovered by accident in 1895, when Wilhelm Röntgen noticed a screen glowing in his lab even though it was shielded from visible light. To convince skeptical colleagues the new rays were real, he exposed a photographic plate to his wife's hand, producing an image of her bones and wedding ring — the first X-ray photograph ever taken.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — 绅 originally named the silk sash worn by officials.
申 (shēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 绅.

士 is thought to picture the head of a battle-axe or a ceremonial weapon planted upright, an emblem of authority carried by an able-bodied man. The sense broadened over time from 'man, warrior' to 'scholar, official, gentleman.'

example.hanzi: 他总是表现得像一位真正的绅士。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì biǎoxiàn de xiàng yí wèi zhēnzhèng de shēnshì.
example.english: He always behaves like a true gentleman.
example.fact: In Victorian England, being a 'gentleman' was defined less by wealth than by not having to work with one's hands for a living; owning land that produced passive income was the real marker of the class. That is why many cash-poor aristocrats still counted as gentlemen while some far wealthier factory owners did not.

components.note: 中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to chóng, sharing the same rhyme.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 花园里爬着一只绿色的虫子。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ pá zhe yì zhī lǜsè de chóngzi.
example.english: A green bug was crawling in the garden.
example.fact: Insects outnumber humans by roughly 200 million to one, and entomologists estimate their combined weight across the planet exceeds that of all wild mammals and birds put together. Ants alone are thought to weigh, in total, about as much as all humans on Earth.

components.note: 厶 (oneself, private) sits above 口 in this ancient, independent character, together once forming an expression of personal satisfaction — 'pleased, content.' That old sense survives only as a faint trace in the pronoun-like archaic use of 台 for 'I.'

口 (mouth) — paired with 厶 above, the mouth completes the old picture of contented speech. The character was later borrowed wholesale as the simplified form of the unrelated 臺 ('platform, stage'), which is the source of 台's modern meaning in 台词.
讠 (speech) — 词 names a word, a unit of speech.
司 (sī) gives the sound — an exact match with 词.

example.hanzi: 演员忘记了下一句台词。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuán wàngjì le xià yí jù táicí.
example.english: The actor forgot the next line.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Hamlet has more lines than any other character he wrote — nearly 1,500 — meaning whoever plays the role speaks for close to 40% of the entire play's running time, one of the most demanding memorization tasks in classical theater.

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
皿 (dish) — 盘 names a flat dish or tray.
般 (bān) gives a sound distantly related to pán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这条街是他们帮派的地盘。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shì tāmen bāngpài de dìpán.
example.english: This street is their gang's turf.
example.fact: Wolves mark their territory with scent from glands between their toes and can defend a range spanning hundreds of square miles. Rival packs typically detect these scent markers long before any face-to-face encounter, which is how wolves avoid most physical fights over land.

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 每个公民都有投票的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi gè gōngmín dōu yǒu tóupiào de quánlì.
example.english: Every citizen has the right to vote.
example.fact: In ancient Athens, citizenship was so restrictive that only free adult men born to two Athenian parents qualified for it. That single rule excluded the majority of the city's population — women, slaves, and resident foreigners — from any political voice at all, despite Athens's reputation as the birthplace of democracy.

meanings: to keep a firm grip on

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抓 describes an action done by hand, grabbing.
爪 depicts claws or fingers gripping something, reinforcing 抓's meaning 'to grab, to seize.'
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'

example.hanzi: 我们得抓紧时间完成任务。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen děi zhuājǐn shíjiān wánchéng rènwù.
example.english: We have to hurry and get the task done without wasting time.
example.fact: Geckos can support many times their own body weight while hanging upside down, thanks to millions of microscopic hair-like structures on their toes called setae. These exploit weak molecular attraction (van der Waals forces) rather than any sticky glue, letting the gecko grip and release instantly with each step.

meanings: seems on the face of it to be

components.note: 手 (hand) — depicts a hand raised above the eyes.
目 (eye) — shielding the eyes with a hand to look into the distance gave 看 its meaning 'to look, to see.'
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 外面看起来快要下雨了。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn kànqǐlai kuàiyào xiàyǔ le.
example.english: It looks like it's about to rain outside.
example.fact: The Müller-Lyer illusion, first described in 1889, makes two identical straight lines look like different lengths just by attaching arrow-like fins to their ends. A ruler proves the lines are equal, but the brain's habit of interpreting the fins as depth cues keeps overriding what is actually there.

components.note: 又 (hand, here standing in for 奚, part of the original character) — a simplified stroke that no longer pictures anything on its own.
鸟 (bird) — combined with the simplified left side, 鸡 names a specific 'kind of bird,' the chicken.
虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.
延 (yán) is only distantly related in sound to dàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 妈妈煮了两个鸡蛋当早餐。
example.pinyin: Māma zhǔ le liǎng gè jīdàn dāng zǎocān.
example.english: Mom boiled two eggs for breakfast.
example.fact: A hen's egg is naturally much stronger against pressure from the top and bottom than from the sides, thanks to its arched shell shape. That design lets a nesting hen sit on and turn a whole clutch of eggs without cracking them, even though her body weight far exceeds what a single shell could take from a sideways push.

components.note: 歹 (death/bad) — 残 relates to damage, destruction, and injury.
戋 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to cán, having drifted apart over time.
刃 (blade) pictures something sharp and painful.
心 (heart) below suggests bearing pain in one's heart, giving 忍 its meaning 'to endure.'

example.hanzi: 这种对待动物的方式非常残忍。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng duìdài dòngwù de fāngshì fēicháng cánrěn.
example.english: This way of treating animals is extremely cruel.
example.fact: The Colosseum in ancient Rome could reportedly be flooded to stage mock naval battles, called naumachiae, complete with warships and condemned combatants fighting to the death for the crowd's entertainment. Historians believe this required an elaborate underground system of channels to flood and drain the arena floor on demand.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 摄 describes taking hold of or capturing something, as in taking a photograph.
聂 (niè) gives a sound distantly related to shè's reading, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) — relates to 像's meaning 'to resemble, be like; image, portrait,' comparing one person or thing to another.
象 (xiàng) gives the sound — 像 is also pronounced xiàng, an exact match.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 电脑上方装了一个摄像头。
example.pinyin: Diànnǎo shàngfāng zhuāng le yí gè shèxiàngtóu.
example.english: A webcam is installed above the computer.
example.fact: The world's very first webcam was pointed not at a person but at a coffee pot in a University of Cambridge computer lab in 1991, so researchers down the hall could check whether it was full before making the walk. The feed stayed live on the early internet until the pot was finally retired in 2001.

components.note: 关 is the simplified form of 關, which drew a gate 門 with a crossbar or bolt threaded through it, barring the way. Simplification dropped the gate radical entirely, leaving only an abstracted version of the crossbar to stand for the whole idea of 'shutting, closing off, a checkpoint.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 请把门关上,外面太冷了。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ mén guānshàng, wàimiàn tài lěng le.
example.english: Please close the door — it's too cold outside.
example.fact: Revolving doors were patented in 1888 specifically to cut heat loss at building entrances, since they never stand fully open the way a hinged door does. Studies of modern building entrances have found a well-used revolving door can lose several times less heated or cooled air than an equivalent swinging door.

components.note: 辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 造's meaning 'to make, build,' an action carried through to completion.
告 (gào) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zào.
土 (earth) — 型 originally related to a mold made of clay used for casting
刑 (xíng) gives the sound — 型 is also pronounced xíng, an exact match

example.hanzi: 她今天的发型造型很特别。
example.pinyin: Tā jīntiān de fàxíng zàoxíng hěn tèbié.
example.english: Her hairstyle today has a very distinctive design.
example.fact: Male peacock spiders perform an elaborate, colorful courtship dance, fanning out iridescent flaps on their abdomen and waving specialized legs in a precise sequence. The display exists purely to shape a visual impression striking enough to persuade a much larger, potentially cannibalistic female not to eat him.

components.note: 子 (child) — 孩 relates directly to children
亥 (hài) gives a sound close to 孩's reading hái
儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 这孩儿长得真可爱。
example.pinyin: Zhè háir zhǎng de zhēn kě'ài.
example.english: This child is really adorable.
example.fact: Human infants are born with a reflexive grasp strong enough to briefly support their own body weight if they cling to a bar or a finger. Researchers consider it a holdover from primate ancestors, whose newborns needed to grip their mother's fur to avoid falling as she moved.

components.note: 又 (hand) and 寸 (also derived from a hand shape) — together suggesting two hands matching or corresponding, related to 对's meaning 'correct, matching.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 两国代表进行了长时间的对话。
example.pinyin: Liǎng guó dàibiǎo jìnxíng le cháng shíjiān de duìhuà.
example.english: Representatives of the two countries held a lengthy dialogue.
example.fact: The Turing Test, proposed by mathematician Alan Turing in 1950, judges machine intelligence purely through open-ended conversation: if a human judge cannot reliably tell whether they're talking to a person or a machine, the machine is said to have passed. Turing originally called it 'the imitation game.'

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 不论天气如何,比赛都会照常进行。
example.pinyin: Bùlùn tiānqì rúhé, bǐsài dōu huì zhàocháng jìnxíng.
example.english: No matter what the weather is like, the match will go on as scheduled.
example.fact: The speed of light in a vacuum measures the same for every observer, no matter how fast they themselves are moving — a strange, experimentally confirmed fact that forms the foundation of Einstein's theory of special relativity. Accepting it forces time itself to run at different rates for observers moving relative to one another.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 镇 originally referred to a heavy metal weight used to press something down, later extending to 'garrison town.'
真 (zhēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 镇's reading zhèn, differing only in tone.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 镇上新开了一家咖啡馆。
example.pinyin: Zhènshàng xīn kāi le yì jiā kāfēiguǎn.
example.english: A new café just opened in town.
example.fact: The small Austrian town of Hallstatt lent its name to an entire early Iron Age European culture after 19th-century archaeologists uncovered thousands of ancient graves near its salt mines. The Hallstatt culture, dated roughly 800 to 450 BC, is now used by historians across Europe as a reference point for that era.

components.note: Originally depicted a hand 扌 gripping a weapon 戈; this original meaning was later borrowed to represent the pronoun 'I/we.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 欢迎你随时来我家做客。
example.pinyin: Huānyíng nǐ suíshí lái wǒjiā zuòkè.
example.english: You're welcome to visit my home anytime.
example.fact: Termite mounds function like a natural climate-control system: their internal network of tunnels channels air currents that keep the colony's core temperature stable within a degree or two, even as the outside temperature swings by more than 20 degrees Celsius between night and day.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
女 (woman) — 姑 names a female relative.
古 (old) — combined with woman, originally suggesting an older female relative, an aunt, giving 姑 its meaning.
女 (woman) — 娘 names a female relative, mother or young woman.
良 (liáng) gives a sound close to niáng, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 那个小姑娘正在公园里荡秋千。
example.pinyin: Nàge xiǎogūniang zhèngzài gōngyuán lǐ dàng qiūqiān.
example.english: That little girl is swinging on the swing in the park.
example.fact: Malala Yousafzai was just 15 years old when she survived an assassination attempt for publicly advocating girls' right to education in Pakistan. Two years later, at age 17, she became the youngest person ever to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water something sinks into
冗 (excess/heavy) — the excess weight that pulls it down
黑 (black/dark) pictures nightfall.
犬 (dog) pictures a dog keeping silent watch in the dark, giving 默 its meaning 'silent, still.'

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息后,他陷入了沉默。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi hòu, tā xiànrù le chénmò.
example.english: After hearing the news, he fell into silence.
example.fact: An anechoic chamber at Orfield Labs in Minnesota holds the Guinness World Record for the quietest place on Earth, absorbing over 99.99% of sound. Visitors report being able to hear their own heartbeat and blood flow once inside, and most people can't tolerate sitting in total silence for more than 45 minutes.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 详 describes speech or an account that is thorough and detailed.
羊 (yáng) shares the rhyme family -ang with xiáng, though the initial has drifted from y- to x- over time.
纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread
田 (tián) gives a loose sound connection to 细's reading xì

example.hanzi: 请把事情的经过详细地说一遍。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shìqing de jīngguò xiángxì de shuō yí biàn.
example.english: Please describe what happened in detail.
example.fact: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter has photographed the Moon's surface in such fine detail that individual bootprints left by Apollo astronauts more than 50 years ago are still clearly visible in its images, along with the paths of the rovers they drove.

components.note: 严 is the simplified form of 嚴, which stacked two mouths (吅, shouting) over a cliff 厂 alongside 敢 ('to dare') — commands barked out from a dangerous, elevated post, an image of discipline under pressure. Simplification kept only a compact shell of that picture.

肃 is the simplified form of 肅, which pictured a hand grasping a tool and working with tight, careful concentration over an intricate pattern. The focus and self-restraint that scene called for carried over into 肃's meaning: 'solemn, respectful, stern.'

example.hanzi: 老师用严肃的语气警告了我们。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yòng yánsù de yǔqì jǐnggào le wǒmen.
example.english: The teacher warned us in a serious tone.
example.fact: The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery has been guarded around the clock, in every kind of weather, without a single interruption since 1937. Sentinels follow a precisely choreographed 21-step walk across the plaza, a number chosen to echo the 21-gun salute, the highest military honor.

components.note: Woman — an old semantic root sometimes linked to feelings.
Gives the sound jiān, related to xián but drifted apart over time.
疋 — a person walking, shown pausing and looking back uncertainly
矢 (an arrow/cane) — an old man's walking stick, held while hesitating
犭 (dog) — 犯 originally related to a dog attacking, later extended to any act of violation
㔾 (jié) gives a sound distantly related to 犯's reading fàn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一名嫌疑犯。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yì míng xiányífàn.
example.english: The police arrested a suspect.
example.fact: Fingerprint evidence became a standard tool in criminal investigation only in the early 1900s. One landmark case came in 1892, when Argentine police official Juan Vucetich matched a bloody fingerprint at a crime scene to a suspect, producing the first criminal conviction in history based on fingerprint identification.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.
豕 (pig/boar) — appears as part of 象's original full-body pictograph of an elephant, reusing a four-legged-animal shape; 象 itself depicts an elephant's trunk and ears above the body.

example.hanzi: 天空出现了暴风雨的迹象。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng chūxiàn le bàofēngyǔ de jìxiàng.
example.english: Signs of a storm appeared in the sky.
example.fact: After the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, wildlife officials in Sri Lanka's Yala National Park found remarkably few animal carcasses compared to the human toll. It led some researchers to suspect that elephants and other animals sensed the coming wave through ground vibrations and fled to higher ground well before it struck.

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

圣 is the simplified form of 聖, which combined an ear (耳, listening) and a mouth (口, speaking) above a standing figure — the image of someone who listens and speaks with special insight, giving 圣 its meaning 'holy, sacred.'

example.hanzi: 教堂里的气氛显得十分神圣。
example.pinyin: Jiàotáng lǐ de qìfēn xiǎn de shífēn shénshèng.
example.english: The atmosphere inside the church felt very sacred.
example.fact: Mount Kailash in Tibet is considered sacred by four separate religions — Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism, and Bon — and, out of respect for that shared religious significance, no one is known to have ever climbed to its summit; mountaineering on the peak is effectively forbidden.

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'

example.hanzi: 一只老鹰在空中盘旋。
example.pinyin: Yì zhī lǎoyīng zài kōngzhōng pánxuán.
example.english: An eagle circled in the air.
example.fact: A Rüppell's griffon vulture holds the confirmed record for highest flight of any bird, after colliding with an airplane at roughly 11,300 meters (37,000 feet) — about the cruising altitude of a commercial jet. The species' blood has an unusually high oxygen-binding efficiency that lets it function in such thin air.

components.note: 广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
亻 (person) — represents a human figure.

叚 depicts borrowing or handing something over — a person who is not genuine, or something borrowed rather than real, gave 假 its meaning 'false, fake' (and, for a break from routine, 'vacation, leave.')

example.hanzi: 我们打算去海边度假一周。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn qù hǎibiān dùjià yì zhōu.
example.english: We plan to go to the seaside for a week's vacation.
example.fact: France was among the first countries to legally guarantee workers paid time off, introducing two weeks of mandatory paid leave in 1936 under the Matignon Agreements. The entitlement has since grown to five weeks and helped establish the modern idea of a paid vacation as a basic labor right across much of Europe.

components.note: 敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
敕 (an order, discipline) — relates to 整's meaning 'orderly, whole, to arrange.'
正 (zhèng) gives a sound hint — 整 is pronounced zhěng, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他为这次考试准备了整整一年。
example.pinyin: Tā wèi zhè cì kǎoshì zhǔnbèi le zhěngzhěng yì nián.
example.english: He spent a whole year preparing for this exam.
example.fact: A solar day and a sidereal day are not quite the same length: Earth actually completes one full 360-degree spin in about 23 hours and 56 minutes, four minutes short of the familiar 24-hour day. Those extra minutes are needed because Earth also has to turn a bit further to catch up with its own movement around the Sun.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 航 relates to traveling by boat, and later by extension, air or space travel
亢 (kàng) gives a sound distantly related to 航's reading háng, having drifted apart over time
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他在一家航空公司当飞行员。
example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā hángkōng gōngsī dāng fēixíngyuán.
example.english: He works as a pilot at an aviation company.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 covered only about 120 feet — shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Brief as it was, it marked the first time in history that a heavier-than-air machine carried a person under its own power.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 探 describes reaching out with the hand to search for something.
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 探长仔细检查了案发现场。
example.pinyin: Tànzhǎng zǐxì jiǎnchá le ànfā xiànchǎng.
example.english: The detective carefully examined the crime scene.
example.fact: London's Metropolitan Police created its first plainclothes Detective Branch in 1842, more than a decade after uniformed officers began patrolling the streets in 1829. The delay partly reflected public unease about police who didn't announce themselves, which many at the time equated with spying.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.hanzi: 士兵接到命令后立刻开火。
example.pinyin: Shìbīng jiēdào mìnglìng hòu lìkè kāihuǒ.
example.english: The soldiers opened fire immediately after receiving the order.
example.fact: During the informal Christmas Truce of 1914, soldiers on opposing sides of World War I's Western Front spontaneously stopped shooting, sang carols across the trenches, and in some sections even played football in no-man's land before the fighting resumed days later.

components.note: The roof-like top of a storage building.
Represents the enclosed space inside, where grain is stored.
广 (shelter) pictures a roofed building.
车 (cart) sits inside, together giving 库 its meaning 'storehouse, warehouse.'

example.hanzi: 这些货物存放在仓库里。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē huòwù cúnfàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
example.english: These goods are stored in the warehouse.
example.fact: Boeing's factory in Everett, Washington, is one of the largest buildings in the world by volume, covering roughly 98 acres under a single roof. It's so large that employees use bicycles and small trains just to move between different sections of the assembly line.

components.note: 士 depicts a scholar or gentleman.
口 (mouth) — the words of a wise, respected person were seen as auspicious, giving 吉 its meaning 'lucky, good.'
亻 (person) plus 也 (also/additionally) — historically meant 'another person,' which developed into the third-person pronoun 'he/him.'

example.hanzi: 他每天晚上都练习弹吉他。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǎnshang dōu liànxí tán jítā.
example.english: He practices playing the guitar every evening.
example.fact: The guitar's ancestors stretch back over 3,000 years to stringed instruments found in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, long predating the modern six-string design that only took its familiar shape in 19th-century Spain, thanks largely to luthier Antonio de Torres Jurado.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 码 originally related to counting stones used for reckoning, extended to mean 'number, code.'
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 码.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 渔船缓缓靠近了码头。
example.pinyin: Yúchuán huǎnhuǎn kàojìn le mǎtou.
example.english: The fishing boat slowly approached the dock.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port every year since 2010, handling more than 47 million shipping containers annually — over three times the volume moved by the busiest port in the United States.

components.note: 阝 (a mound/city) — represents a place being traveled to.
迶 depicts walking or moving along a path — following someone to the city gave 随 its meaning 'to follow, along with.'

目 (eye) anchors the bottom of 着, a modern simplification of 著. The 'watching, arriving at a visible state' sense behind it fed into 著/着's meaning of settling into or continuing in a state — the root of its modern job marking an action still in progress.

The upper element is a worn-down remnant of the phonetic component 者 (zhě) that sat atop 艹 in the original 著. Centuries of simplification flattened it into a shape that no longer functions as either a live sound or meaning cue on its own.

example.hanzi: 随着科技的发展,生活越来越方便。
example.pinyin: Suízhe kējì de fāzhǎn, shēnghuó yuè lái yuè fāngbiàn.
example.english: With the development of technology, life is becoming more and more convenient.
example.fact: Starling flocks perform a phenomenon called a murmuration, in which thousands of birds shift direction almost simultaneously. Researchers have found each bird isn't reacting to the whole flock at once — it's simply tracking and instantly following the movements of its seven closest neighbors, which is enough to make the whole group move as one.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
至 (zhì, to arrive) — carries 到's core meaning, 'to reach, to arrive'
刂 (a form of 刀, dāo) gives a sound close to 到's pronunciation dào

example.hanzi: 请把书放到桌子上。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fàngdào zhuōzi shàng.
example.english: Please put the book onto the table.
example.fact: The Crypt of Civilization at Oglethorpe University in Georgia, sealed shut in 1940, is often called the first modern time capsule. It isn't scheduled to be opened until the year 8113 — nearly 6,000 years after it was placed there, chosen to mark an equal span of time before and after the start of the Egyptian calendar.

components.note: 工 (work, tool) — 巧 relates to skill in craft or work.
丂 (kǎo) gives a sound close to qiǎo.
亼 pictures a lid or cover, its converging strokes showing something coming down to close over an opening.
口 (an opening, mouth of a vessel) sits beneath the lid; a cover fitting snugly over the container's mouth gave 合 its meaning 'to close, fit together, unite.'

example.hanzi: 我们在同一天生日,真是巧合。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài tóng yì tiān shēngrì, zhēnshi qiǎohé.
example.english: We have the same birthday — what a coincidence.
example.fact: The 'birthday paradox' shows that in a random group of just 23 people, there is better than a 50% chance two of them share a birthday. Most people badly underestimate this because they instinctively compare their own birthday to everyone else's, rather than counting every possible pair in the group.

components.note: 山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.
女 (woman) — 姆 names a woman who cares for children.
母 (mǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 姆's reading mǔ.

example.hanzi: 山姆每天早上都去跑步。
example.pinyin: Shānmǔ měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
example.english: Sam goes jogging every morning.
example.fact: The American nickname 'Uncle Sam' is generally traced to Samuel Wilson, a meatpacker who supplied barrels of beef stamped 'U.S.' to American troops during the War of 1812. Soldiers reportedly joked that the initials stood for 'Uncle Sam' Wilson himself, and the nickname for the country stuck.

components.note: 酉 (a wine vessel) — 配 originally related to blending or mixing wine
己 (jǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 配's reading pèi, having drifted apart over time
亼 pictures a lid or cover, its converging strokes showing something coming down to close over an opening.
口 (an opening, mouth of a vessel) sits beneath the lid; a cover fitting snugly over the container's mouth gave 合 its meaning 'to close, fit together, unite.'

example.hanzi: 团队成员之间配合得很好。
example.pinyin: Tuánduì chéngyuán zhījiān pèihé de hěn hǎo.
example.english: The team members cooperate very well with each other.
example.fact: Cleaner wrasse fish run informal 'cleaning stations' on coral reefs, where much larger predatory fish line up and hold perfectly still while the wrasse picks parasites off their skin and even out of their mouths and gills — a mutual arrangement that benefits both species without the predator eating its cleaner.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 称/稱 originally described weighing grain on a scale, a sense that widened into 'to weigh' and, since things get sorted by weighing them, eventually 'to call, to name.'
爯 (chēng) depicts a hand lifting an object to weigh it, and its reading matches 称/稱's own exactly — later simplification reshaped the right side of the character beyond easy recognition.
口 (mouth) — 呼 describes an action of the mouth, such as calling out or breathing.
乎 (hū) gives the sound — an exact match with 呼.

example.hanzi: 你可以直接称呼我的名字。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zhíjiē chēnghu wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: You can just address me by my first name.
example.fact: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for over 70 years, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history when she died in 2022. During that single reign, thirteen different U.S. presidents and fifteen different British prime ministers came and went while the formal address for the British sovereign remained unchanged.

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那位女子正在图书馆看书。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi nǚzǐ zhèngzài túshūguǎn kànshū.
example.english: That woman is reading in the library.
example.fact: Marie Curie remains the only person of any gender to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911 — for her pioneering research on radioactivity, a term she herself coined.

components.note: 八 (two hands) — holding something up.
目 (a container/tray) — held between the two hands, the image behind 具's meaning 'tool, utensil.'
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.

example.hanzi: 这种材料具有防水的功能。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng cáiliào jùyǒu fángshuǐ de gōngnéng.
example.english: This material has a waterproof function.
example.fact: Axolotls possess a remarkable regenerative ability: they can regrow entire lost limbs, sections of their spinal cord, and even parts of their heart and brain without forming any scar tissue. That ability has made them one of the most heavily studied model organisms in regenerative medicine research.

meanings: (coll.) admirable, impressive (usu. in 好样的, 'way to go')

components.note: 女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 面对困难还能坚持下去,真是好样的。
example.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnán hái néng jiānchí xiàqù, zhēnshi hǎoyàng de.
example.english: Being able to keep going in the face of difficulty — now that's admirable.
example.fact: Junko Tabei survived being buried in an avalanche partway up a mountain in 1970, and just five years later, in 1975, became the first woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest. She went on to become the first woman to complete the Seven Summits, climbing the highest peak on every continent.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.

example.hanzi: 就算失败了也没什么大不了的。
example.pinyin: Jiùsuàn shībài le yě méi shénme dàbuliǎo de.
example.english: Even if we fail, it's really no big deal.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, built into an Arctic mountainside, was engineered to survive almost any worst-case scenario, including a direct nuclear strike. It currently holds backup samples of more than a million crop seed varieties, insurance against the possibility of a global agricultural catastrophe.

components.note: 刂 (a knife, related to 刀) — ties to 刚's meaning 'firm, hard, strong'
冈 (gāng) gives the sound — 刚 is also pronounced gāng, an exact match
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 这双鞋的尺寸刚好合适。
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de chǐcùn gānghǎo héshì.
example.english: This pair of shoes fits exactly right.
example.fact: Earth orbits the Sun within what astronomers call the 'Goldilocks zone,' the narrow band of distance where temperatures are just right for liquid water to exist on a planet's surface. Climate models suggest that moving Earth even a few percent closer to the Sun could trigger a runaway greenhouse effect that boils away the oceans entirely.

components.note: 木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 申请人必须本人到场办理手续。
example.pinyin: Shēnqǐngrén bìxū běnrén dàochǎng bànlǐ shǒuxù.
example.english: The applicant must be present in person to complete the procedures.
example.fact: Very few animal species reliably pass the mirror self-recognition test, which checks whether an animal understands it's looking at its own reflection rather than another individual. Only a handful of species — including great apes, dolphins, elephants, and Eurasian magpies — have been shown to pass it convincingly.

components.note: 衤 (cloth) — 补 means to mend or patch clothing.
卜 (bǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 补.
亻 (person) — 偿 describes a person repaying something owed.
尝 (cháng) is an exact match for the sound of 偿.

example.hanzi: 公司决定给受影响的顾客一些补偿。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng gěi shòu yǐngxiǎng de gùkè yìxiē bǔcháng.
example.english: The company decided to give the affected customers some compensation.
example.fact: Many people who lose their eyesight show measurable improvement in their remaining senses, a phenomenon researchers call sensory compensation. Brain-imaging studies have found the visual cortex — normally dedicated to processing sight — gets recruited to help process sound and touch instead.

components.note: 忄 (heart, mind) — 忏 (to repent) is an inner, emotional act.
千 (qiān) gives a sound only distantly related to chàn today, a connection that has faded over roughly three millennia of sound change.
Heart — regret is an emotional response.
Gives the sound měi, related to huǐ but drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 他在信中表达了深深的忏悔。
example.pinyin: Tā zài xìn zhōng biǎodá le shēnshēn de chànhuǐ.
example.english: In the letter, he expressed deep repentance.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up in 1995 after the end of apartheid, offered perpetrators of political violence amnesty from prosecution in exchange for a full public confession of their crimes. The restorative-justice model it pioneered has since been studied and partly adapted by more than 40 other countries.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 跟 originally referred to the heel of the foot, extended to mean 'to follow (on someone's heels)'
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 跟's reading gēn

目 (eye) anchors the bottom of 着, a modern simplification of 著. The 'watching, arriving at a visible state' sense behind it fed into 著/着's meaning of settling into or continuing in a state — the root of its modern job marking an action still in progress.

The upper element is a worn-down remnant of the phonetic component 者 (zhě) that sat atop 艹 in the original 著. Centuries of simplification flattened it into a shape that no longer functions as either a live sound or meaning cue on its own.

example.hanzi: 小狗一直跟着主人跑来跑去。
example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu yìzhí gēnzhe zhǔrén pǎo lái pǎo qù.
example.english: The little dog kept following its owner around.
example.fact: Konrad Lorenz's studies of graylag geese in the 1930s revealed 'imprinting': goslings will follow the first moving object they see after hatching and treat it as their mother. In his most famous demonstrations, goslings imprinted on Lorenz himself and followed him everywhere, work that later earned him a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize.
